subject: Automotive & EVs
title: How Seatbelts Actually Work
description: A 60-second lesson on How Seatbelts Actually Work.

hook.text: A seatbelt seems like a simple strap, but the engineering inside is surprisingly clever.

buildup.text: The retractor uses a spool and spring that lets you lean but locks during sudden motion.

discovery.text: A tiny pendulum sensor detects rapid deceleration and jams the spool in milliseconds.

twist.text: Modern pretensioners use small explosive charges to yank the belt tight the instant a crash starts.

climax.text: Load limiters then release just enough slack so the belt doesn't crack your ribs on impact.

punchline.text: Seatbelts tighten and loosen in a single crash.

quiz.question: What do pretensioners do during a crash?
